rationale: Repair of trial-b04d1d014e's measured failure, not a repeat of its explanation. The previous joint selection at the two c10d::allreduce_ functional sites breached step_ms (256.98 ms vs 138.66 limit) while its mechanism actually worked: the separately collected objective runs measured communication_kernel_sum_ms at median max-rank 63.5 ms (rank samples 60.3/62.1/66.2 and 65.6/63.5/63.5) versus the 74.676 ms baseline. The binding_cost collector on that revision isolates the breach cause: the parent arm ran 139.58/139.86 ms while the binding-only passthrough (candidate computation omitted, the two functional sites retained) ran 253.08/231.30 ms - about +92..113 ms of pure binding cost. With the request's frozen binding_backend=legacy, unscoped functional sites take the global dispatch path over every operator of the invocation (binding-contract.md), and python_runtime pstats confirm it: kernel_optimizer binding __torch_dispatch__ intercepted 7563 ops per step (~29 ms self plus ~12 ms torch._ops __str__, ~7 ms find_torch_dispatch_rule, ~9.4 ms dict.get), destroying the host/device overlap this co-saturated eager step depends on; the gloo barrier itself added only ~+4 ms (screened 257 ms vs passthrough 253 ms; the 18.5 ms single-barrier pstats entry is cProfile/dispatch-polluted). Therefore the repair must keep the validated alignment mechanism while eliminating functional dispatch entirely. The 13 allreduce_ dispatches (12x 7,087,872-element buckets closed by the 39,385,344-element embedding bucket, execution_timeline seq 21-33) are issued by DDP's C++ reducer during the final backward with the project invoke 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (target project.invoke, no parents, both ranks, 1 invocation per step) as their only call parent, so no module boundary contains them; the single project call is the one coherent editable boundary that is installed as a direct callable with zero functional sites and zero global dispatch overhead. The candidate replaces exactly that call with a faithful re-execution of the measured step (same zero_grad/no_sync accumulation loop over state['inputs'], same loss scaling, same phase markers, same SGD step and final torch.cuda.synchronize, same return values, executed from live state on every invocation) plus one addition: a single gloo barrier on the adapter's existing state['control'] group issued from the main thread immediately before the final microbatch's loss.backward() - the last safe host point before the collective burst, with the autograd engine idle, unlike the failed engine-thread placement. Measured justification that this term is reducible: the current execution_timeline shows the leading rank dispatching the burst 6.25-7.29 ms (bounds) before the peer, its first NCCL kernel running 9.702 ms against the 3.275-3.675 ms peer/floor (collective_calibration: 3.593 ms for 7,087,872 elements, 19.642 ms for 39,385,344, i.e. a ~62.76 ms per-rank synchronized floor), and hooked rank sums of 64.08/70.56 ms against a 74.676 ms clean baseline max-rank. A barrier at the same group the adapter's out-of-timer before_run already uses emits no NCCL kernels and cannot perturb the communication collector; it converts device spin-wait into a bounded host wait that the trailing rank - which paces the 132.06 ms baseline max-rank wall - never pays. Bytes, DDP flags, bucket layout, algorithm, transport, op order and arithmetic stay untouched, so bit-exact gradient replicas and all reference checks are preserved. The earlier execution_plan CUDA-graph attempt is not revived: its capture failure and allocator inflation are already on record and the graph route is not needed to reach the floor.
hypothesis: To be tested, not assumed. Predicted: aligning both ranks' hosts immediately before the synchronized backward removes the pre-burst component of the 6.25-7.29 ms cross-rank submission offset, so the leading rank's first bucket kernel falls from ~9.7 ms toward the ~3.3-3.6 ms floor and later kernels stay near floor except for intra-burst re-growth; communication_kernel_sum_ms (median of 3 profiled repeats, max rank) should drop from 74.676 ms to roughly 63-67 ms (~10-16%), consistent with the 63.5 ms already measured for burst-start alignment and the 62.76 ms synchronized floor. step_ms should stay under the 138.66 ms limit (expected ~132-137 ms): the replacement adds no dispatch overhead (direct callable, no TorchDispatchMode), the barrier's clean base cost is sub-ms, and the leading rank's wait is bounded by the same skew its kernels previously absorbed, partially hidden behind its already-queued GPU work. Explicit unknowns the framework's measurement must decide: (a) the clean-run skew magnitude - every timeline number is hook-perturbed, so the wait converted into step_ms may be smaller or larger than 6.25-7.29 ms, and only the ~+4 ms binding_cost delta estimates it cleanly; (b) residual skew re-developed between the barrier and the first bucket and across the burst (0.4-3.9 ms in the hooked after-trace) bounds the gain short of the floor; (c) the gloo barrier's own clean latency on this control group has never been measured unprofiled; (d) the objective's run-to-run spread (baseline repeats 72.4-79.9 ms) means acceptance rests on the median, not any single predicted value; (e) if the barrier raises or fails, the candidate must fall back to the exact parent step semantics so correctness, bit-exact replicas and the negative control are unaffected - the barrier touches no tensors, so numerics are invariant by construction.
